title: Install your AI agent
caption: Your first command: copy it, paste it into your terminal, press Enter.
paste: Open your terminal from step 1, paste this line and press Enter. It installs your AI agent.
docsWhy: Always there, even if this line ever changes. Some install pages need scrolling, so the line is here.
powershellHint: On Windows, use PowerShell: its prompt starts with PS C:\.

unixFailure: The installer command failed? Check that your computer is selected above and that you pasted the whole line into your terminal. For a company restriction, stop and ask IT.

claude-code.one: On Windows, 'irm' is not recognized means you are in Command Prompt: open PowerShell, or use the Command Prompt line above.
claude-code.two: Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan. The free plan does not include it, and the sign-in in the starter folder says so.

antigravity.one: On Windows, 'irm' is not recognized means you are in Command Prompt, not PowerShell: open PowerShell and paste again.
antigravity.two: The line stops with red text: that is what Help is for.

codex.one: A line that does not fit your computer fails at once: check that the right system is picked above.
codex.two: The line stops with red text: that is what Help is for.

copilot.one: GitHub Copilot needs an active Copilot subscription on your GitHub account; without it, the sign-in in the starter folder fails.
copilot.two: On Windows, GitHub asks for PowerShell 6 or higher, and winget must exist. A message saying it is not recognized: use Help.

helpLine: Stuck, or red text you do not understand? Press Help at the top right and paste the error.
worked: After the installer finishes without errors, close the terminal, open a new one and run this check:
versionWorked: You see a version number, not an error. Then continue to Your folder. If the command is still not recognized, open More help below.

workLaptop.title: Work laptop? Check before you install.
workLaptop.mac: If macOS asks for an administrator password, stop and ask IT or your workshop organizer.
workLaptop.windows: If Windows asks for an administrator password, stop and ask IT or your workshop organizer.
workLaptop.linux: If Linux asks for sudo or an administrator password, stop and ask IT or your workshop organizer.
workLaptop.text: Use an agent and account your organization approves. Stop for company blocks or certificate errors too. Do not turn off security settings or switch networks to get around a block.

windows.claude-code: Claude's native Windows installer does not need administrator rights. You still need your organization's approval on a work laptop.
windows.copilot: Use PowerShell 7, not the built-in Windows PowerShell 5.1. GitHub requires PowerShell 6 or newer. If PowerShell 7 or winget is missing or blocked, ask IT to provide them and Copilot before the workshop.
windows.codex: On a work laptop, ask IT to approve this command first: it includes -ExecutionPolicy ByPass. Later Windows sandbox setup may also ask for administrator approval. Do not disable the sandbox to continue.
windows.antigravity: On a work laptop, have IT approve Antigravity's CLI installation and account first. Installing into your user folder does not mean company policy permits it.
windows.version: Not sure which PowerShell you have? Type $PSVersionTable.PSVersion and press Enter. The number under Major is the version; a prompt starting with PS alone does not tell you.

enterprise.title: Blocked on a company laptop?
enterprise.network: A Zscaler block page, certificate error or connection timeout may need different fixes. Ask IT to check the agent's approved sites, proxy and corporate certificate. A working browser does not prove the agent can connect.
enterprise.policy: “Running scripts is disabled”, “blocked by your organization”, missing winget, or an administrator-password request: stop. Do not change execution policy, disable certificate checks or install a different tool to bypass the block.
enterprise.handoff: Tell IT which agent you chose, your PowerShell version, the step and the exact error. Remove tokens, personal information and confidential details before sharing an error or screenshot. Ask them to verify installation, sign-in and a harmless agent request before workshop day.

windows-prerequisites.description: Anthropic documents a native Windows installer without administrator rights and optional Git Bash [1]. GitHub requires PowerShell 6+, whereas Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 are separate installations [2][3]; this guide recommends a current PowerShell 7 for Copilot. OpenAI's official Windows install command includes a process execution-policy override [4]. Google documents agy and its version check [5]. Codex's Windows sandbox source includes elevated provisioning, separate from user-scoped CLI installation [6]. These are documentation-verified instructions, not a clean-PC or managed-Windows test.

corporate-network.description: Anthropic separates proxy, certificate and endpoint configuration [1]. GitHub discusses corporate certificate trust and Zscaler, and maintains a separate allowlist [2][3]; this does not certify every CLI with every Zscaler deployment. Microsoft gives organizational Group Policy precedence over local execution-policy settings [4]. Stopping and asking IT is this guide's safety recommendation, not a promise that every block has one fix.

your-first-command.title: Your first command
your-first-command.script: This is the first command you type in your terminal. It installs your AI agent. Pick your computer and your AI agent in the toolbar, and the page shows you the exact line. Press the big Copy button, paste into your terminal and press Enter.

official-docs-always.title: Official docs, always
official-docs-always.script: Next to the line is a button to the official docs of your AI agent. I give you the line so you do not have to scroll through a page that has no anchor, but the vendor is the source, so if the line ever stops working, the docs are one click away.

what-you-will-see.title: What you will see at the end
what-you-will-see.script: At the end of the install, your terminal may ask you a question. For Codex on Mac and Linux it is Start Codex now, with y or N: type N and press Enter, because you start it later, inside the starter folder. For GitHub Copilot, answer y if it asks to add itself to your shell file. For Claude Code you see Installation complete. Whichever agent you picked, do not start it yet: its first start happens inside the starter folder, so it only sees your workshop files.

what-might-happen.title: What might happen
what-might-happen.script: Before installing on a work laptop, make sure your organization approves the agent and account. Administrator prompts, company blocks and certificate errors are reasons to stop and ask IT, not to change security settings. Check the Windows prerequisites shown for your agent, and use the fresh-terminal version check after installation. More help explains the common blockers. Remove confidential information from errors before sharing them.

codex.one: On Mac and Linux the last line asks Start Codex now? [y/N]. Type N and press Enter: you start it later, inside the starter folder.
codex.two: Typed <key>y</key> already? Codex starts here, outside the folder. Quit it with <key>Ctrl</key> <key>C</key> and go on; you start it again inside the starter folder.

claude-code.one: The installer ends with Installation complete. If a Setup notes block talks about your PATH, follow the fix it prints there.
claude-code.two: Don't start it yet: you start claude for the first time inside the starter folder, two Slides on.

copilot.one: On Mac and Linux it may ask Would you like to add it to … ? [y/N]. Type y and press Enter.
copilot.two: The last line says copilot help. Don't start copilot yet: you start it for the first time inside the starter folder.
